correctness.rationale: Universal VC at most two follows from intersecting-incomparable trace obstruction. Positive membership classes are inclusion chains of at most H concepts, proving the online upper bound. Complete b-ary regular trees realize all ancestor-chain thresholds, and an opposite root subtree supplies matching negative rank by induction. The n<=4 bound follows from 2N concept counting and a two-shape binary-tree analysis; a five-leaf explicit root (2,3) split gives rank three. Two independent combinatorial generators reproduce the complete 1–5-leaf census and regular-tree finite instances.

value.rationale: A natural hierarchy-encoded hypothesis space has a sharp all-height upper bound independent of the potentially enormous number of clusters, matched across every complete regular branching number. A complete pair-shattering polynomial remains fixed by leaf count whereas online complexity depends on depth; the five-leaf onset identifies the exact first adaptive gain. These are mathematically motivated hierarchy complexity questions, not arbitrary finite parameter slices; the infinite-family proof makes the dimension separation unbounded.
